slot.topic_title: Setting Up a Test for the Difference Between Two Population Means

item.title: Setting Up a Test for Two Fertilizers
item.stimulus: A farm cooperative believes a new fertilizer gives a greater mean corn yield than the standard fertilizer. Thousands of fields in the region use each fertilizer. The cooperative independently and randomly selected 36 fields that use the new fertilizer (sample mean 48.6 bushels per acre, standard deviation 6.4) and 40 fields that use the standard fertilizer (sample mean 45.9, standard deviation 7.1).

parts.prompt: Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of all fields in the region that use the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of all fields in the region that use the standard fertilizer.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of all fields in the region that use the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of all fields in the region that use the standard fertilizer, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and show that its conditions are met.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the fields were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of fields.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the fields were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of fields.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of fields that use its fertilizer.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of fields that use its fertilizer.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of all fields in the region that use the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of all fields in the region that use the standard fertilizer. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means, Randomization: the fields were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of fields. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of fields that use its fertilizer. Sample-data condition: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.
item.verification_python:
n1, n2, m1, m2 = 36, 40, 48.6, 45.9
assert min(n1, n2) >= 30
assert m1 > m2
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")

item.title: Setting Up a Test for Two Fertilizers

Its researchers randomly assigned 36 plots to the new fertilizer (sample mean 48.6 bushels per acre, standard deviation 6.4) and 40 plots to the standard fertilizer (sample mean 45.9, standard deviation 7.1).

parts.prompt: Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of plots treated with the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of plots treated with the standard fertilizer.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of plots treated with the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of plots treated with the standard fertilizer, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and show that its conditions are met.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means, because two independent samples of quantitative values are compared and the population standard deviations are unknown.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means and gives the reason: two independent samples of quantitative values are compared and the population standard deviations are unknown.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks randomness and independence: the plots were randomly assigned to the two fertilizers, so the two groups are independent.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context and, when sampling, the 10% condition: the plots were randomly assigned to the two fertilizers, so the two groups are independent.
criteria.fix: Check the data came from random sampling or random assignment, and for sampling that the sample is under 10% of the population.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean yield, in bushels per acre, of plots treated with the new fertilizer, and μ₂ is the true mean yield of plots treated with the standard fertilizer. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means, because two independent samples of quantitative values are compared and the population standard deviations are unknown. Randomization and independence: the plots were randomly assigned to the two fertilizers, so the two groups are independent. Sample-data condition: both sample sizes (36 and 40) are at least 30.

The part only asks students to identify the procedure and verify its conditions; identifying the two-sample t-test should earn the procedure point without this additional justification.
